## Report

<https://github.com/HaydenRAllen/ec422_ps2_allen>

```{r}
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```
## Data

The data is unemployment rates across the country (USA) and some specific states. It comes from the St. Louis Federal Reserve Bank (FRED) between the years 1976 - 2026. 

```{r} 
#| echo: false 

unemp_raw = read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds") 
unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      symbol == "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
      symbol == "ORUR" ~ "Oregon",
      symbol == "CAUR" ~ "California",
      symbol == "TXUR" ~ "Texas",
      symbol == "NYUR" ~ "New York"
    )
  )

unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      symbol == "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
      symbol == "ORUR" ~ "Oregon",
      symbol == "CAUR" ~ "California",
      symbol == "TXUR" ~ "Texas",
      symbol == "NYUR" ~ "New York"
    )
  )

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(
    unemployment_rate = replace( 
      unemployment_rate,
      date == as.Date("2025-10-01"),
      unemployment_rate[date == as.Date("2025-09-01")]
      )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(unemployment_rate, date) |>
  group_by(date) |>
  mutate(unemployment_rate_change = unemployment_rate - lag(unemployment_rate)) |>
  ungroup()

head(unemp)

```



## Wrangling



The table below is a few statistics using data from the unemployment data (mean rate, minimum rate, and maximum rate).
```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_summary <- unemp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate = min(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate = max(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

kable(unemp_summary)

```



The table below removes all data prior to 2015 and shows us only recent data.
```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_recent <- filter(unemp, date >= as.Date("2015-01-01"))
unemp_recent_summary <- unemp_recent |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate = min(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate = max(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

kable(unemp_recent_summary)

```



The table below shows us the top unemployment rate increases not including the year covid started.
```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_top_increases_no_covid <- unemp |>
  filter(format(date, "%Y") != "2020") |>
  group_by(region) |>
  slice_max(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(desc(unemployment_rate_change))

kable(unemp_top_increases_no_covid)

```



The table below shows us the top unemployment rate decreases not including the year covid started.
```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_top_decreases_no_covid <- unemp |>
  filter(format(date, "%Y") != "2020") |>
  group_by(region) |>
  slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(unemployment_rate_change)

kable(unemp_top_decreases_no_covid)

```


## Visualization

```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate Over Time",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Unemployment Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
The graph above is showing the unemployment rate over time for the different states/the entire country on one graph.
```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ region) +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate Over Time by Region",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Unemployment Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
The graph above shows the employment rate over time for the different states/the entire country on separate graphs.
```{r}
#| echo: false
ggplot(unemp_summary, aes(x = (fct_reorder(region, mean_rate)), y = mean_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Average Unemployment Rate by Region",
       x = "Region",
       y = "Average Unemployment Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
The graph above shows the average unemployment rate from 1976 to 2026 for the different states/the entire country.
```{r}
#| echo: false
unemp_covid <- unemp |>
  filter(format(date, "%Y") == "2020")
ggplot(unemp_covid, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate During COVID-19 Pandemic",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Unemployment Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
For this graph I used the unemp_covid data frame, which filters the unemployment data 
to only include the year 2020. This allows us to focus on the impact of the COVID-19 
pandemic on unemployment rates across different regions. You can notice that New York pea after everyone else.
